outOfScope: HTTP methods, status codes, and request mechanics

claims.claim: HTTPS is HTTP carried over TLS, with TLS providing encryption and authentication for client-server communication.
TLS 1.3 is designed to prevent eavesdropping, tampering, and message forgery in Internet client-server communication.
HTTPS protects a client-server connection but does not establish that all site content is accurate or that an application has no other security defects.
A securely loaded page that fetches resources through HTTP or another insecure protocol has mixed content, whose insecure resources can be viewed or modified in transit.
Browsers mitigate mixed content by upgrading some insecure resource requests to HTTPS and blocking other insecure request types, but secure sites should avoid mixed content.
A certificate warning should be treated as a reason to pause and independently verify the destination before supplying sensitive information, rather than a routine bypass prompt.
